result.title: NearFormer: Linear-Size Sparse Attention via Randomized Near Neighbors
result.summary: Graph transformers can capture long-range interactions, but their quadratic attention cost limits their use on large graphs. We introduce \emph{NearFormer}, a graph transformer whose global attention is restricted to a randomized near-neighbor (NN) graph. NearFormer uses an efficient randomized construction to connect each node to a small number of near neighbors from a broader neighborhood defined by a label-independent feature or spectral geometry. For a fixed retained budget \(k\), the resulting attention support has linear size \(\mathcal{O}(|E|+nk)\). The NN graph is built once by within-bin search and then held fixed. We use these edges as sparse global-attention supports, with optional learned attention biases, while preserving the original graph for local message passing. Experiments on long-range graph benchmarks and synthetic structural tasks show that NearFormer provides a favorable accuracy--scalability trade-off relative to local message passing, dense and sparse attention.

AI.brief_summary: 该文提出 NearFormer：一种图 Transformer，用一次性构造的随机近邻图作为全局注意力的稀疏支撑，把注意力规模压到线性，并与保留原图的局部消息传递配合，在长程图基准上考察精度与可扩展性的折中。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「用随机近邻构造固定稀疏注意力支撑」的做法可能供核查：能否以低成本为 VLM 的长程注意力预先筛选参与计算的状态或视觉证据，从而影响 latent 相似度与计算分配，但图节点设定与原论文的收益尚未在视觉推理上验证。
